_comment: The machine mirror of docs/design/SECURITY_NEGATIVE_TEST_MATRIX.md, which declares 242
negative test IDs and, until this file, bound them to nothing: exactly ONE of the 242
appeared anywhere in .rs/.py/.ts source. A declared obligation nothing establishes is the
defect shape this repository gates against, so the matrix is now an artifact a check reads.
GENERATED by tools/generate_negative_matrix.py from the markdown. Do not hand-edit the
id set, under_test or section -- they are re-derived and a hand edit is reverted. status,
test, blocked_on and reason are the judgements and ARE preserved across regeneration.
implemented  -- a test exists, names the ID in its function name and carries the ID as a
string in its body, and goes RED when the control it tests is removed.
Every one was mutation-verified: the control was broken, the test was
observed failing, and the control was restored.
blocked      -- the code under test does not exist in this tree. blocked_on names what
must exist first. This is NOT 'we did not get to it'.
unreviewed   -- nobody has established this row against the tree. It is NOT a pass and
never was. It is the honest default for a plan retrofitted onto a tree.
unreviewed_baseline freezes the debt. tools/check_negative_matrix.py refuses any ID that is
unreviewed and not listed there, so a NEW markdown row cannot arrive as silent debt: it
fails the gate until someone either reviews it or adds it to the baseline in a visible diff.

NM-TIME-13.blocked_on: The §7 lease-time invariant `completed_at_ms ≤ lease_expires_at_ms` is not implemented anywhere on the verify path. MEASURED 2026-09-19 against the real ledger (in-memory SQLite via engine/tests/test_negative_matrix.py fixtures): after `_executing()`, `record_completion(conn, 'att-1', _produced(completed_at_ms=lease_expires_at_ms + 1), 40, derived=_derived())` returned `created`, the row moved to `COMPLETED`, and `load_attestation_state` returned terminal state with completed_at_ms=1210001 against lease_expires_at_ms=1210000 — the §4.9 attestation input IS built for a completion past lease expiry; the matrix requires `lease_expired` and no envelope. What must exist first: a check that reads the acceptance row's `lease_expires_at_ms` and refuses `completed_at_ms` past it — in `governed_supervisor_ledger.record_completion` / `governed_supervisor_server.complete_governed_run` (the only functions that hold both values), or a `lease_expires_at_ms` evidence field plus a limb in `isolated_signer._check_timestamps` — surfacing as governed `lease_expired`. This is a gap in a shipped control, reported rather than papered over; closing it is a change to audited security code that this work is not authorised to make.

NM-TIME-14.blocked_on: The row's fault cannot be injected: `finished_at_ms` does not exist anywhere in the tree (zero source occurrences), and `started_at_ms` exists only as win-live's `execution_started_at_ms`, which the Windows twin compares to `completed_at_ms` in `admit_completion` (servers.rs:610-627) — a different inequality on a different field, already tested at servers.rs:2015. `build_execution_receipt` (engine/runtime/governed_supervisor.py:742-761) emits no started/finished fields at all. What must exist first: the §4.7 `started_at_ms`/`finished_at_ms` fields on the execution receipt (recorder-stamped, `started ≤ finished`) and a §7 chain-inequality check over the full four-term chain; until then the only chain checks are the two ends (`accepted ≤ completed` in the signer/broker, `execution_started ≤ completed` in win-live).

NM-REG-02.blocked_on: The §7 durable registry floor tuple does not exist as code. The only floor is a bare integer, `OpenConfig.registry_epoch_floor: int = 0` (engine/runtime/governed_turn_open.py:220), handed to `challenge_key_registry.resolve_registry` (governed_turn_open.py:459, governed_acceptance.py:717) whose single floor comparison is `payload['registry_epoch'] < epoch_floor` (challenge_key_registry.py:394) — no hash, no handle. MEASURED 2026-09-19 against the real module: a document with `registry_epoch == epoch_floor` (7 == 7) resolves to a snapshot with reason None whatever its content, so a same-epoch/different-hash registry (and any handle) is admitted at the floor. `grep -rn highest_registry_epoch` over engine/ and apps/desktop/src-tauri (non-target) returns zero source hits (the literal exists only in the addendum at :3450); engine/runtime/supervisor_ledger.sql has no registry-floor table (its only floor table is `governed_evidence_head_floor`, :168); `registry_hash`/`registry_handle` outside challenge_key_registry.py appear solely as acceptance-row provenance columns. `bro_signature.resolve_registry_floor` is the tool-signing registry's `registry_version` pin — a different artifact; binding this row to it would test a control the row does not describe. What must exist first: a durable supervisor floor row persisting `(highest_registry_epoch, registry_hash, challenge_registry_handle, root_key_id)` per addendum §7 (:3448-3453), and a `resolve_registry` floor comparison that refuses a differing `registry_hash` at `registry_epoch == floor`. This is a gap in a shipped control, reported rather than papered over.

NM-MAN-04.blocked_on: The `key_usage: receipt_signing | supervisor_attestation` discriminator on `ManifestKey` (§1.6) and a receipt-key resolver that rejects `key_usage != receipt_signing` (§1.7). MEASURED: `key_usage` has zero occurrences in any .rs/.py/.ts/.tsx/.json/.sql/.sh under apps/desktop/src-tauri, apps/desktop/src, engine, bridge, contracts, config and tools; `ManifestKey` (key_manifest.rs:26-37) is key_id/public_key_hex/trust_class/valid_from_ms/valid_to_ms/key_epoch/revoked/allowed_protocols. The signer and the supervisor-attestation key are resolved by the identical `resolve_production_key(.., RECEIPT_ENVELOPE_ARTIFACT_TYPE, ..)` predicate (manifest_resolver.rs:208-211; win-live resolver.rs:243-251; config.rs:231-246) and the attestation key is provisioned as a production receipt-protocol key (config.rs:388-394; manifest_resolver.rs:328-330), so no manifest-level control distinguishes the two kinds. The pinned-id check at governed_verification.rs:906 is a config binding, not the type separation this row names.

NM-MAN-05.blocked_on: `resolve_attestation_key(supervisor_attestation_key_id, supervisor_id, now_ms)` (§1.7) and the `key_usage` field it would reject on — neither exists. MEASURED: `resolve_attestation_key` and `key_usage` each have zero occurrences in any .rs/.py/.ts/.tsx/.json/.sql/.sh under apps/desktop/src-tauri, apps/desktop/src, engine, bridge, contracts, config, tools. The supervisor-attestation key is resolved by `resolve_production_key(&manifest, &sup_attest_key_id, RECEIPT_ENVELOPE_ARTIFACT_TYPE, now)` (manifest_resolver.rs:210; win-live resolver.rs:245-251; config.rs:238-246), i.e. by exactly the predicate a receipt-signing key satisfies, so a receipt-signing key used for attestation is accepted by design in this tree. What must exist first: the usage discriminator on `ManifestKey` (key_manifest.rs:26-37) and a distinct attestation resolver that refuses `key_usage != supervisor_attestation`.

NM-FRAME-06.blocked_on: A registry-bytes canonicality gate — the artifact-#2 analogue of `governed_turn_open._canonicality_gate` — does not exist. `challenge_key_registry.resolve_registry` (:355) takes an already-parsed `Mapping` (`validate_registry_document` :305 refuses anything else; raw bytes → `registry_unknown`, measured) and RECOMPUTES `document_bytes = canonical_bytes({payload, root_sig})` at :397, so `registry_handle` is derived from the re-encoding and the transported bytes are never compared to it; the production loader `run_ladder_supervisor.load_tcb_json` :637-639 is `json.load(fh)` with no byte check, and no Rust code parses `brops.challenge-key-registry.v1` at all. MEASURED 2026-09-19: an `indent=2` and a key-reordered registry document both resolve to a full snapshot with `reason=None` and a handle equal to the CANONICAL hash, not the hash of the bytes given. What must exist first: a registry ingress that strict-decodes the file BYTES (`brops_protocol.strict_loads`) and refuses when `bytes != canonical_bytes({payload, root_sig})` — e.g. a `resolve_registry_bytes(document_bytes, ...)` seam wired into `resolve_registry_document` — so the handle the supervisor binds into the acceptance row (governed_acceptance.py:411) is the hash of the bytes it actually read. That is a change to the audited §4.2 resolver, not a test.

The reply that exists today is the frozen `brops.sign-result.v1` op reply; its readers are bounded at 262144 (`brops_protocol.MAX_FRAME_BYTES`, reached from `brops_socket.request` :135 — the supervisor's path), 524288 (`isolated_signer_server.MAX_FRAME_BYTES` :64) and 8192 (`ipc_framing::MAX_FRAME_PAYLOAD_BYTES`, broker `recv_all`/`read_one_reply` chain_executor.rs:668, :686) — no 65536 sign-result bound exists (`grep -rn 65536` hits only containment-evidence and generation-config caps). What must exist first: the §4.5 frame's validator carrying `MAX_SIGN_RESULT_BYTES = 65536` on the supervisor's signer-reply path (with the ≈9865-byte worst-case fixture the row names), consumed by `AcceptanceDriver._attest_and_sign` (governed_acceptance.py:877).
